pure-announcement.rationale: An ICLR 2026 research paper describing a coordination method, not a launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: No supplied nearest concept touches multi-LLM coordination; the closest material is the sibling staging note on the RL Conductor, which uses a different optimization (RL topology design) than Trinity's evolutionary role assignment.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Backed by a primary arXiv/ICLR paper with named benchmarks and a described architecture a reader can check.

durability.rationale: The lasting content is the trade-off analysis — a tiny coordinator assigning Thinker/Worker/Verifier roles, and separable CMA-ES beating RL under strict budget and high dimensionality — which outlives the quoted 86.2% LiveCodeBench score.

actionability.rationale: Adopting Trinity means training an evolved coordinator, so for most readers it informs the design space (roles, ES-vs-RL choice) rather than giving a directly executable practice.

atomicity.rationale: One idea — a lightweight evolved coordinator that delegates per-turn roles across heterogeneous LLMs — with the ES analysis as supporting evidence, statable in one paragraph.
